claims.statement: All curated tool modules live flat under agent/tools/ and are re-exported through agent/tools/__init__.py, which lazily imports and caches each export from _TOOL_MODULES; its custom _LazyToolsModule prevents same-named imported submodules from shadowing public tool exports.

A single tool module can back multiple exported names — for example both background_execute and background_task map to .background_execute, and the four environment tools (capture_environment_snapshot, delete_environment, list_environments, save_environment) all come from .environments.

deepagents.create_deep_agent contributes the built-in filesystem, shell, and subagent tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, delete, ls, glob, grep, execute, task), tracked in server.py as DEEP_AGENT_TOOL_NAMES; these must not be duplicated as curated tools.

The main agent's default tool set excludes the built-in grep (DEEP_AGENT_EXCLUDED_TOOLS), and stop-summary mode additionally strips the mutating built-ins delete, edit_file, execute, task, and write_file (STOP_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED_TOOLS).

agent/server.py:get_agent assembles the main coding agent's static_tools list covering web, plan lifecycle, background execution, user configuration, Linear, thread, baby-sit, notification, PR creation/review, scheduling, Slack, and user-facing sandbox helpers.

The main agent's tool list is dynamic: admin threads add ADMIN_TOOLS, sandbox download tools are added only when enabled, local_run collapses to just http_request/fetch_url/web_search, stop_summary_mode collapses to slack_read_thread_messages/slack_thread_reply, and Slack tools are removed when Slack is not enabled.

Admin threads gain ADMIN_TOOLS — sandbox_reset, environment management (list_environments, save_environment, capture_environment_snapshot, delete_environment), and organization-skill management (save_organization_skill, delete_organization_skill).

The main agent exposes Observability, Currents, Notion, and optionally Corridor as DynamicToolMiddleware integration groups, so the model must call load_integration_tools before a requested integration tool is added to a later model turn; group loading is deferred and failures are returned as tool errors rather than failing the run.

agent/reviewer.py:get_reviewer_agent wires curated review tools fetch_review_diff, add_finding, update_finding, list_findings, publish_review, resolve_finding_thread, reply_to_finding_thread, plus web_search, fetch_url, and http_request; it does not wire open_pull_request as a curated reviewer tool.

agent/analyzer.py:get_analyzer runs a minimal graph exposing only save_review_style_prompt (the save_review_style module export) and read_finding_outcomes, the latter used in continual mode to refine the per-repo review-style prompt from prior finding outcomes.

agent/chat.py defines a separate sandbox-less 'chat with this PR' agent for the review UI that uses GitHub-API-backed read tools (read_repo_file, search_repo_code), list_review_findings, and web tools, operating over PR context seeded as virtual /pr/ files.

read_repo_file and search_repo_code read repository source over GitHub Contents/code-search APIs using repo coordinates and chat_github_token from run config; PrepareChatRunMiddleware obtains that token from the GitHub App installation for the sandbox-less chat graph.

list_threads, get_thread, and manage_thread (agent/tools/threads.py) are parent-agent-only thread-management tools that derive the acting user from trusted run configuration, recheck allowed-organization membership, and preserve the dashboard's owner/participant/admin authorization checks rather than trusting thread metadata.

Plan mode is enforced by PlanModeMiddleware using PLAN_MODE_EXCLUDED_TOOLS; it is installed unconditionally and is state-aware, so it restricts mutating tools even after a mid-run enter_plan_mode call, not only when a run starts in plan mode.

PLAN_MODE_EXCLUDED_TOOLS removes side-effecting curated tools during planning — including task, background_execute/background_task, create_sandbox_service_url, http_request, open_pull_request, request_pr_review, manage_thread, manage_baby_sit, sandbox_reset, recreate_sandbox, mutating Linear tools, user-skill mutations, Slack moves/new threads, and environment mutations — while list_threads, get_thread, and built-ins write_file/edit_file/execute remain available.

http_request routes outbound HTTP through url_safety redirect protection and treats large responses by writing them into the sandbox rather than inlining, and its docstring directs the agent to use gh in the sandbox for GitHub API calls instead of this tool.

background_execute launches non-blocking commands in the thread sandbox with bounded concurrency and output (MAX_ACTIVE_TASKS=4, MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=1MiB) and timeout limits, tracking task state under TASK_ROOT in the sandbox.

fetch_review_diff materializes the current review diff into the reviewer's sandbox and returns only bounded metadata (a file path plus limited fields), so the reviewer inspects the diff with grep/read_file rather than fetching the full diff through execute or gh.

schedule_thread_wakeup schedules a future re-invocation of the agent thread via the LangGraph SDK, bounded by minimum/maximum delays and a cap on consecutive system wakeups between user messages, so a thread can resume itself without a new user message.

manage_code_channel implements the Slack channel-per-task session, keyed via the CODE_CHANNEL_SESSION_TS sentinel, covering channel creation, status, commands, views, canvases, and archival through the Slack agents.sessions/conversations APIs.

Agent/UI parity is a stated product principle: any dashboard UI capability should generally also be reachable through an agent tool subject to the same authorization and safety boundaries, so new UI capabilities should add or extend the corresponding curated tool.

Adding a new tool follows a fixed process: add the module to agent/tools/, export it from agent/tools/__init__.py, and wire it into the tools=[...] list in server.py:get_agent (or reviewer.py for reviewer-only tools); implementations are async-only.

Open SWE keeps its toolset intentionally small and curated rather than accumulating tools, performing GitHub operations via gh in the sandbox and content search via rg through execute instead of adding dedicated tools.

Individual tools are covered by focused unit tests under tests/tools/, including test_background_execute.py, test_threads.py, test_schedule_thread_wakeup.py, test_http_security.py, and test_manage_baby_sit.py.

enter_plan_mode persists planning status when possible and returns a Command setting plan_mode true, while approve_plan validates active non-shared plan state, records approval identity, and returns a Command setting plan_mode false.
The PR-chat proxy seeds virtual overview, diff, and findings files for a PR and enforces that every client-supplied chat thread belongs to the requesting login and the same repository and PR.

manage_baby_sit rejects PRs outside the configured repository and, before starting a watch, requires an executable thread, an open PR with head information, GitHub authentication, and a GitHub App installation.

open_pull_request prefers a triggering user's OAuth token for Slack, Linear, and dashboard sources, falls back to the GitHub App token, and returns an existing branch PR rather than creating a duplicate.
